extra.message: User-controlled searchText is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to db.all(). searchText originates from the POST body field searchText (routes/search.js:11, req.body.searchText) and the GET query parameter searchText (routes/api.js:7, req.query.searchText). Because the value is embedded inside single quotes without escaping or parameterization, an attacker can break out of the string literal and manipulate the query (e.g., '%' OR 1=1 --), enabling SQL injection. A parameterized version of the query is even present as a comment on the following line (line 7), confirming the intended fix.

Reflected XSS: the template uses the unescaped output operator '!=' to render 'Search Results for: ' + searchText. searchText is fully attacker-controlled (from req.body.searchText in routes/search.js:11) and is echoed back by searchService (service/search.js:17) into ret.searchText. Because pug's '!=' does no HTML escaping, an attacker who submits e.g. <script>alert(document.cookie)</script> as the search text has it executed in the victim's browser. Use '=' (escaped interpolation) instead of '!='.

Information disclosure (CWE-209): the error handler always exposes the raw err object (including stack trace) whenever req.app.get('env') === 'development'. Because express defaults env to 'development' when NODE_ENV is unset (the app is started via 'npm start' with no NODE_ENV), internal error details and full stack traces are rendered to end users via views/error.pug:6 (pre #{error.stack}). This can leak internal file paths, dependency versions, and code structure to attackers, aiding further exploitation.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Information disclosure: when the underlying SQL query fails, the raw sqlite3 error object (err) is serialized straight into the HTTP response via res.json(err). The error messages produced by sqlite3 can include the malformed SQL statement and database schema details, which leaks information that is useful for crafting further SQL injection payloads.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded credentials (CWE-798): the database bootstrap seeds a well-known admin account 'admin' with the plaintext, hardcoded password 'S3cr37P@$$w0rD!' (and further weak passwords for user1-user3 on lines 44-46). These credentials are stored unhashed in the SQLite database and are trivially discoverable in source code, allowing anyone to authenticate as a seeded user if authentication is enabled.
